name: AudioDER
description: Recent advances in pretrained large audio-language models (LALMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities across speech, sound, and music. To adapt these models to downstream tasks without the cost of pretraining from scratch, post-training has become a widely adopted paradigm. However, the effectiveness of post-training depends critically on the quality of the training corpus. We observe that existing post-training corpora, often constructed by aggregating public audio datasets, suffer from substantial acoustic redundancy, as many of these datasets are sourced from overlapping media platforms.
